solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Rock, something round to bulge out as seen from behind

indicators.note: viewing from behind means the pieces are read from back to front

parts.note: an orb is a sphere or globe
to bag is to swell or bulge, like baggy trousers

explanation.surface: A geologist describes a rock whose rounded shape seems to swell when viewed from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as seen from behind' turns ORBBAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabbro is a dark, coarse-grained igneous stone, an example of a rock.

clue.text: Party organised by adults completely pointless

indicators.note: the compass points west, north and south are all removed, leaving the word with no points at all

parts.note: adults are grown-ups

explanation.surface: A gathering arranged by grown-ups turns out to be utterly purposeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' plays on compass points: W, N and S are each taken out of GROWNUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A party in the political or social sense is a faction or band of people acting together.

clue.text: Explosive buried under mountain peak to yield clay

indicators.note: the explosive sits below the mountain in this down entry, so it comes second

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis
tonite is a blasting explosive made from guncotton

explanation.surface: Blasting charges set beneath a summit expose a seam of clay.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is Scottish for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Bentonite is an absorbent volcanic-ash clay used in drilling muds and cat litter.

clue.text: Dope ranting, not entirely effective

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: A fool's ranting is only partly persuasive.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant is a formal word for something that operates or produces an effect.

clue.text: What could be seen as part of recipe, arid!

definitions.text: What could be seen as part of recipe, arid!

parts.words: What could be seen as part of recipe, arid
parts.note: inside the words recipe, arid the letters PE and A are parted by the comma, so a pea is seen divided

explanation.surface: Something dry that appears in a cooking recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The dried pulse suits 'arid', but the real trick is visual: the comma splits the letters of 'pea' inside 'recipe, arid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A split pea is a dried pea halved, a staple of soups and a natural recipe ingredient.

clue.text: Cor, the mysteries about one branch of a particular science!

definitions.text: one branch of a particular science

indicators.note: about means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how puzzling one area of a science can be.
explanation.definitionFit: This field studies the three-dimensional arrangement of atoms in molecules, a branch of chemistry.

clue.text: American plants raised in rows

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: rows are lines
something raised is up

explanation.surface: Plants from the Americas grown in neat rows.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the US spelling of lupins, flowering plants of the pea family.

clue.text: Full of sex appeal, was model put forward?

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it inside

parts.note: a model poses, so was model gives posed
it is an old term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Asks whether an alluring model was pushed into the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a proposition or assumption.

clue.text: A Sun scare unlikely to engender feeling of confidence

indicators.note: an unlikely arrangement suggests these letters must be reordered

explanation.surface: A tabloid scare story is not going to make readers feel safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; 'unlikely' rearranges A SUN SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurance is self-confidence or certainty, a feeling of being sure.

clue.text: Foreign city in which nothing's tightly packed

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
dense means tightly packed

explanation.surface: A city abroad where nothing is crowded.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is a Danish city, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen.

clue.text: Weight gained from a combination of pies and mash

indicators.note: combining the two words means their letters are mixed together anew

explanation.surface: Putting on weight after eating pie and mash.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie and mash is a traditional London dish; 'a combination of' shuffles PIES and MASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight in the sense of importance or stress laid on something.

clue.text: Silly talk when port's been drunk in the monk's office

indicators.note: a drink taken in goes inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: prate is foolish chatter
Rio de Janeiro is a port city, Rio for short

explanation.surface: Foolish chatter in a monastery office once the port has gone round.
explanation.definitionFit: A priorate is the office or term of a prior, a monk heading a priory.

clue.text: It could be bird compound with name at front

indicators.note: placed at the front means the name letter comes first

parts.note: an ester is a chemical compound

explanation.surface: A bird might be a chemical compound with a name attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A nester is one that builds or occupies a nest, which a bird could be.

clue.text: Religious festival faces criticism, not quite bringing things together

indicators.note: the festival faces the criticism, so it comes in front

parts.note: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours

indicators.note: the final letter is lopped off the word for criticism

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in getting stick

explanation.surface: A religious festival comes under fire, yet nearly unites people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the K from STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Holistic thinking treats the parts of something as an integrated whole.

clue.text: One part of Switzerland bathed in exceptional heat for winter

indicators.note: surrounded by, so one piece sits inside the other
exceptional suggests these letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Bern is a Swiss canton and the capital

explanation.surface: A Swiss region under a heatwave, as the season of cold approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' rearranges HEAT to HATE, and 'bathed in' places IBERN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter as a verb means to spend the cold season somewhere, as hibernating animals do.

clue.text: Bring down old nurse to hug tot

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A former nurse cuddling a toddler is somehow depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone down is to depress them, making them unhappy.

clue.text: Believers in force using Military Intelligence to infiltrate rulers

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: dynasts are hereditary rulers

explanation.surface: Supporters of violence use spies to get among the ruling families.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamists hold the philosophy of dynamism, that force or energy underlies all matter.

clue.text: What Jolson's mother did in a northern region

parts.note: a mother bore her child
Al Jolson was the singer and star of The Jazz Singer

explanation.surface: A question about what the entertainer Jolson's mother did.
explanation.walkthrough: What Al Jolson's mother did was bear Al: BORE AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Boreal means situated in or relating to the north, as in boreal forest.

clue.text: Super maiden in torn dress

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: rent means torn
A1 means super or first-class, written here as AI
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A wonderful young woman wearing ripped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 stands as AI, the digit 1 read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Shrub in ground, mostly brown, beginning to atrophy

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: land is ground
tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A plant in the soil, browning and starting to wither.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantana is a tropical flowering bush of the verbena family.

clue.text: Lions cavorting in this place, not the foremost place for play

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other
the leading letter is dropped

parts.note: here means this place

indicators.note: cavorting suggests leaping around, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lions leaping around a stage location, though not at its front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests sport or frolicking lions, but it means a stage drama; 'not the foremost' beheads the word for this place, and 'cavorting' jumbles the big cats inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the Danish castle where Shakespeare's Hamlet is set.

clue.text: What's laid out on table for crossword compiler's job

definitions.meaning: a place laid with cutlery and glasses at a dinner table
composing a puzzle is called ... it

explanation.surface: Table arrangements contrasted with the work of a puzzle-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a place arrangement at table, and the act of composing a crossword.

clue.text: Stirrin' up something in the cake-making mix?

definitions.meaning: stirring up is raising, here with its last letter clipped as in casual speech
a dried grape added to fruit cake

explanation.surface: Stirring the batter in the bowl, hoping something is in there.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G in 'Stirrin'' signals the same clipping in the synonym raising.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisins are dried grapes, a common ingredient in cakes and buns.

clue.text: Like some games Ian Smith played

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Games that a man called Ian Smith took part in.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Smith was the Rhodesian prime minister; 'played' rearranges his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isthmian Games were ancient Greek athletic contests held at Corinth.

clue.text: It's next (just the northern half) to China

definitions.text: It's next (just the northern half) to China

indicators.note: in a down entry the north is the top, so only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a pal

explanation.surface: A country described as lying beside China, at least on the northern side.
explanation.walkthrough: China is also Cockney slang: china plate rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom borders Tibet, the Chinese region to its north.

clue.text: Morally deviating President facing right angry tirade

indicators.note: the president faces the rest, so comes in front

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US President
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A president on the receiving end of a furious diatribe about his morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means departing from the accepted standard of conduct.

clue.text: Agreeing with others is arch

definitions.meaning: being in harmony with the group, marching in time
the raised part of the foot between toes and ankle

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means in agreement; as one, the arched middle of the foot.

clue.text: Request to have food placed in foyer?

indicators.note: putting one thing in another makes a container

parts.note: an entry is an entrance hall or foyer
eat, as in eats, is informal for food

explanation.surface: Asking to have something to eat brought to the lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or appeal.

clue.text: Attempt to read out bit by bit short account of holy life

parts.note: a go is an attempt

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to spell is to name letters one by one

explanation.surface: Trying to read aloud, piece by piece, a brief life of a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last L from SPELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the four New Testament Gospels recounts the life of Christ.
